input.note:
**Cause**: The ledger-export cronjob is being terminated due to exceeding the `activeDeadlineSeconds` deadline of 3600 seconds (1 hour). The job logs show it was processing batches of ledger data and was terminated at 02:00:04Z (1 hour after start), while still processing batch 69/95. This results in job status "Failed: DeadlineExceeded".

**Evidence**: Pod logs show the job started at 01:00:04Z and received SIGTERM at 02:00:04Z after 1 hour. The job specification shows `activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600` [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/job#job-termination-and-cleanup-1]. According to Kubernetes documentation, when a Job reaches `activeDeadlineSeconds`, all running Pods are terminated and the Job status becomes `type: Failed` with `reason: DeadlineExceeded` [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/job#job-termination-and-cleanup-1].

**Fix**: Increase the `activeDeadlineSeconds` value in the ledger-export CronJob spec to allow more time for the job to complete. Calculate the required time based on the current processing rate (69 batches in ~1 hour suggests roughly 8.3 minutes per 10 batches, so 95 batches would need ~79 minutes total). Set `activeDeadlineSeconds` to at least 5400 seconds (90 minutes) or higher to provide a safety margin. The job must be updated at the CronJob resource level, as `activeDeadlineSeconds` applies to each Job instance created by the CronJob.
